prompt_en: Photorealistic night-ferry engine-room documentary, medium-wide and slightly low-oblique. One unmistakably adult marine engineer is the primary subject; recognizable facial structure, skin tone, hairstyle, and adult age presentation follow Image 1. Image 1 is the sole appearance and identity source. Show a verified-safety relief display: verified-safety relief immediately after a non-graphic bilge-pump alarm. An inactive alarm remains visible as a fading amber beacon beside the dry inspection port, and the engineer checks an analog pressure gauge whose needle sits clearly in the green band. The adult reads the safe gauge indicator while the analog pressure needle sits clearly in the green band, as an adult colleague points to a steady green status light and nods. Only after the check, both of the engineer's shoulders visibly drop, the jaw unclenches, the eyelids soften, and the gloved hand relaxes its grip. The engineer's shoulders visibly drop while the jaw loosens, the eyelids soften, and the gripping hand releases the torque wrench. The adult lowers the emergency tool, a torque wrench, and resumes the safe task by marking a clipboard checklist. Cool overhead fluorescence and restrained amber spill model the face, gauge, damp steel, confirmation partner, and lowered tool in one clear focal hierarchy.
